name: Onboard & Launch Company
description: Flagship end-to-end onboarding: gather brand + business info from the public site, import the product catalog FIRST (so the theme renders real products), then clone the site into a Fluid theme through small, individually-QA'd build steps (scrape/assets, tokens/skeleton, header/footer, homepage, product/collection templates, content pages + push), iteratively refine against paired screenshots, reconcile onboarding info, discover UGC, and deliver a live-verified launch-readiness review. QA on each step grades against explicit hard-fail bars — cosmetic gaps become notes for the refine pass, not run-killers.

steps.name: Gather brand & business info
acceptance: The company's website was crawled and the legal/business name, support contact, and business hours (where publicly listed) were located and reported.
Brand assets (logo URL, primary brand colors, fonts) were identified and captured for downstream steps.

Whatever onboarding/business fields could be pre-filled via the Fluid API were submitted (HIGH + MEDIUM confidence only) using the EXACT contracts in onboarding/onboarding-prefill/references/api-endpoints.md. Field pushes are BEST-EFFORT: a field whose push still fails after retrying with the documented endpoint/payload (e.g. a support email or rename returning 400) is recorded in STEP_OUTPUT.remaining_for_human with the endpoint + error and does NOT fail this step. LOW-confidence fields were reported but not pushed.
The step's STEP_OUTPUT includes the canonical website_url the rest of the workflow will use.

HARD-FAIL BAR (the only reasons this step may fail): the website could not be crawled at all, the active company could not be confirmed, or NOT A SINGLE field could be pushed. Individual field failures — however many — are remainders, not failures; a failed root step cascades and kills every downstream step, so reserve failure for total blockage.

steps.name: QA brand + business data before the build
steps.prompt:
Independently verify the data gather-context produced BEFORE the product import and theme build consume it — a wrong brand color, missing font, or wrong market propagates into every theme section and the store config. Re-fetch from the API and check against the SOURCE site; do not trust gather-context's self-report. Exact brand_guidelines contract (allowed fields incl. logo_url; PATCH body wrapped in the brand_guidelines key; logo/icon/favicon must be DAM URLs uploaded first via dam_upload): see onboarding/onboarding-prefill/references/api-endpoints.md.

1. Brand (drives the theme): GET /api/settings/brand_guidelines. Confirm primary/secondary/accent colors are SET (not defaults/placeholders) and match the source site's actual palette (sample the source CSS/logo). Confirm brand fonts were IDENTIFIED for the theme build (brand_guidelines has NO font field — do not fail QA for a missing font on that endpoint; fonts land in theme tokens).
2. Countries/markets (drive currency, locale, tax, theme): GET the company countries; confirm the intended market(s) are configured with correct currency/locale.
3. Business info: only when push_business_data is in scope, confirm legal/business name, support contact, business hours (where public) landed; otherwise brand+countries correctness alone is required.
4. Loop: for any field wrong/missing and recoverable from the source, fix it (re-push) and re-verify; else record it.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { brand:{colors,fonts,source_match}, countries:[...], business:{...}|'out-of-scope', status:'pass'|'cap-reached', remaining_for_human:[...] }.
acceptance: Brand colors + fonts were verified against the SOURCE site (not merely 'set') — the palette handed to the theme build matches the source. A wrong/default palette that is fixable from the source this turn should be FIXED and re-verified, not failed.
The intended market country/countries are configured with correct currency/locale.
If push_business_data is in scope, business fields landed and were re-verified; otherwise brand+countries correctness alone is confirmed and business marked out-of-scope.
STEP_OUTPUT reports status 'pass' or 'cap-reached' with an itemized remaining_for_human list — no silent pass.

HARD-FAIL BAR: grading is against OUTCOMES AVAILABLE DOWNSTREAM, not push mechanics. A value that failed to persist via settings but is correctly RECORDED in STEP_OUTPUT for downstream steps (e.g. brand color the theme build applies directly) plus listed in remaining_for_human is acceptable — do not fail the run over a field-level 400. FAIL only when the brand palette is wrong/unverified against the source AND unrecoverable this turn, or the intended market cannot be determined.

steps.name: Import products (Connect / scrape / manual)
steps.prompt:
Import the company's product catalog into Fluid. This step runs BEFORE the theme build on purpose — the theme's product and collection templates render REAL products, so the catalog must exist first. The manager step context includes a `products_source` field set by the fronting `onboarding/onboard-launch-company` skill — branch on it:

**Case A — `products_source: "connect"`**
  A Connect droplet (Shopify / Exigo / ByDesign / Pillars / Infotrax) was chosen. The context also has `connect_provider` (slug) and `connect_droplet_uuid`.
  1. GET /api/droplets/{connect_droplet_uuid} and confirm `is_connected: true`. If not, drop through to Case B and note the switch in your report.
  2. Trigger the droplet's product-sync entrypoint. Providers today expose different sync verbs (Shopify: `POST /api/droplets/{uuid}/sync?resource=products`; others: check the droplet's own actions). If unsure, GET /api/droplets/{uuid} and read `settings.actions` for the sync endpoint.
  3. Poll GET /api/company/v1/products until the count stops climbing (or 60 s elapses), then report the final count from `meta.pagination.total_count`.

**Case B — `products_source: "scrape"`**
  1. Using `website_url` from the gather-context step output, locate the site's product/shop pages via the crawl tool. For Shopify-backed sources, `<site>/products.json?limit=250` (paginated) is the fastest source of truth. FILTER OUT app-helper junk before counting or importing: $0 products, subscription-upsell/cashback helpers (Aftersell 'Upgrade to Quarterly', Fondue 'CashBack', ymal/crosssell, test products) — importing those makes the store look broken.
  2. Create each product with the NESTED-ATTRIBUTES payload (a flat `{product:{title,price}}` shape silently creates $0 shells — pricing lives on variant_countries):
     POST /api/company/v1/products with `{ "product": { "title", "description", "active": true, "status": "active", "images_attributes": [...], "option_attrs": [names...], "variants_attributes": [ { "is_master": true, "option_attrs": [values...], "variant_countries_attributes": [ { "country_iso": "US", "currency_code": "USD", "price": <n>, "compare_price": <n|null> } ] }, ... ] } }`. Exactly one variant has `is_master: true`. Product-level `option_attrs` are option NAMES, variant-level are VALUES (lengths must match; a lone 'Default Title' variant gets none).
  3. Images: upload each source image via POST https://upload.fluid.app/upload with `external_asset_url` (the server fetches the remote CDN image) or the dam_upload tool, then reference `asset.default_variant_url` in `images_attributes`. Never hotlink source CDNs.
  4. NOTE: Fluid re-slugifies from the title and may append a uuid to every slug — match existing products by TITLE with slug-prefix fallback, and use each created product's canonical_url/slug from the API (not the source handle) when linking. Idempotency: GET /api/company/v1/products first and skip products that already exist — match by SLUG with title fallback (Fluid re-slugifies from title and appends a uuid on collisions, so title-only matching undercounts).
  5. Report source-count vs created / skipped / failed with product ids, using `meta.pagination.total_count` (never the returned array length — pagination caps it).

**Case C — `products_source: "manual"`**
  1. Create exactly one stub product with title 'Sample Product', description 'Replace me before launch.', price 0. This unblocks onboarding without pretending the catalog is real.
  2. Explicitly report 'MANUAL ENTRY REQUIRED for N products' and list what was found on the site (from a light crawl) so the human has a checklist.

Always end with STEP_OUTPUT that includes: products_source used, `meta.pagination.total_count` after this step, source-vs-created counts, any failures, and — for Case C — the list of products the human still has to add.
acceptance: GET /api/company/v1/products `meta.pagination.total_count` returns at least one product after this step (real for A/B, stub for C).

For Case A/B: imported products are `status: "active"` with a non-zero price on the default country's variant pricing and at least one image on the Fluid DAM (spot-check 3 via the API — do not trust the report).
For Case A/B: the created/skipped/failed counts in the report are consistent with what the API returns; no duplicate slugs were created; $0 app-helper junk was excluded, not imported.
For Case C: the report explicitly says 'MANUAL ENTRY REQUIRED' and names how many products need human entry.
The step's STEP_OUTPUT records which branch ran (`products_source`) so later steps can grade coverage accordingly.

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only when NO product exists after the step, or imported products are broken at the spot-check level ($0 shells with no pricing, zero images across the board, or still draft). A shortfall vs the source count (some products failed/skipped) is a remainder for the report, not a failure — record it in STEP_OUTPUT.remaining_for_human.

steps.name: Theme 1/6 — scrape source + section inventory + DAM assets
steps.prompt:
First theme step. You are in a scaffolded Fluid base-theme project (the orchestrator created it from the base-theme starter). Call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") to load the full clone playbook, then execute ONLY its discovery phases for `website_url` from the caller context: page discovery (Step 4), content scraping (Phase 1), visual audit (Phase 2), and image extraction + DAM upload (Phase 3). Do NOT build sections or templates yet — later steps own that.

Scope tightly so this stays fast and achievable:
- Page manifest capped at: homepage, global nav + footer, 1 collection/shop page, up to 3 representative product pages, up to 4 key static pages (about/faq/contact/policies).
- Section inventory REQUIRED for: homepage (every section, with layout/colors/fonts/spacing notes from computed styles) and the global header + footer. Other pages: a one-line structure sketch each is enough.
- Images: download + dam_upload every image the homepage, header/footer, and the sampled PDPs/collection actually need (use parallel dam_upload calls). Record `asset.default_variant_url` for each.
- Fonts: extract the real @font-face families/files; note licensing (importable vs needs-substitute) per the skill's fonts section.
- Reconcile brand colors/fonts with the gather-context step output; the source site wins on conflict (note the conflict).

Write everything to `clone-manifest.json` at the theme project root: { source_url, page_manifest:[...], section_inventory:{...}, brand_tokens:{colors,fonts,licensing_notes}, dam_assets:{<source_url>:<dam_url>} }. Later steps read this file instead of re-scraping.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: manifest path, page count, homepage section count, images uploaded count, brand tokens summary, and any pages/assets you could not capture (as notes, not failures).
acceptance: `clone-manifest.json` exists at the theme project root and contains a page manifest, a homepage + header/footer section inventory with concrete style values, brand tokens (colors + fonts with licensing notes), and a source-URL → DAM-URL asset map — verify by READING the file, not the worker's claim.
Spot-check 2-3 DAM URLs from the manifest: they resolve to real images (HTTP 200).
The section inventory covers every visible homepage section (compare against the live source homepage).

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only when the source site could not be scraped at all, the manifest file is missing/empty, or zero images landed on the DAM despite the source clearly having images. Missing individual pages, sections noted as 'could not capture', or a partial asset map are NOTES for later steps — not failures.

steps.name: Theme 2/6 — design tokens + skeleton boots
steps.prompt:
Wire the source site's design tokens into the theme so every later section references them. Call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") and execute ONLY Phase 4b (Theme Config Setup) using `clone-manifest.json`'s brand_tokens:

1. `config/settings_data.json`: set the 12-color palette + 5-font palette + heading sizes from the manifest (every font slot seeded — defaults in settings_schema.json do NOT auto-apply to missing keys).
2. `config/settings_schema.json`: confirm every color/font setting carries its `option_group` (background_colors / font_families) — sections' dropdowns are empty without them.
3. `layouts/theme.liquid`: all 12 `--clr-*` and 5 `--ff-*` CSS variables wired in :root with `| default:` fallbacks. If the source font is importable, add the @font-face (note the licensing disclaimer in a comment); otherwise use the manifest's chosen substitute and note it.
4. Honor the caller context's `theme_target`: `new` → this scaffolded project is the target; `existing` with `theme_id` → record that id as the push target for later steps. Record the decision in clone-manifest.json under `theme_target_resolved`.
5. Boot the dev preview (`fluid theme dev`) and take a screenshot_preview to confirm the skeleton renders (base-theme placeholder content is fine at this point).

End with STEP_OUTPUT: tokens set (colors/fonts), font licensing decision, theme_target_resolved, and dev preview status.
acceptance: settings_data.json + settings_schema.json parse as valid JSON; the 12 color slots and 5 font slots are populated with the manifest's brand values (not base-theme defaults), and every color/font setting has its option_group.
layouts/theme.liquid wires all --clr-* and --ff-* variables with | default: fallbacks; the font decision (real @font-face or named substitute) is recorded.
The dev preview boots and renders without server errors — verified with a screenshot_preview this turn (placeholder content is acceptable; this step is about tokens + skeleton, not content).

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only when a config file is invalid/unwritten, tokens still hold base-theme defaults, or the dev preview cannot boot. Imperfect color mapping or a debatable font substitute is a NOTE for the refine pass.

steps.name: Theme 3/6 — header, navigation & footer
steps.prompt:
Build the global chrome: `sections/main_navbar` and `sections/main_footer` matched to the source site's header/footer using clone-manifest.json (inventory + DAM assets). Call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") for the section architecture rules (Section Shell + Container, blocks for content, tokens not hex, canonical blocks/components).

Requirements:
- Navbar: source's logo (DAM URL), nav items mirroring the source's top-level navigation but pointing at FLUID routes (/home, /home/collections/<slug>, /home/pages/<slug> …); working mobile hamburger; PRESERVE Fluid's JS hooks verbatim (#show-cart, #fluid-cart-count, #show-language-country-dropdown, .saveLocaleBtn, .country-selector, .language-selector — the canonical navbar components own these; render them, never rewrite).
- Footer: source's column structure, social links, legal links, newsletter block if the source has one.
- Audit gate: run `python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` on both section files and fix EVERY violation before finishing.
- Verify in the dev preview with screenshot_preview at desktop AND mobile widths.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: sections written, audit result, nav items mapped (label → route), and any deviations from the source recorded as notes for the refine pass.
acceptance: main_navbar and main_footer exist, render in the dev preview without Liquid errors (check the dev server log), and visibly correspond to the source's header/footer structure (logo, nav items, footer columns).
Fluid's cart/locale JS hooks are intact in the navbar (grep for #show-cart, #fluid-cart-count — their absence breaks cart + locale switching store-wide).
`python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` passes (exit 0) on both section files.
A mobile-width screenshot shows a working hamburger/collapsed nav state.

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only for Liquid errors, missing sections, destroyed JS hooks, or unfixed audit violations. Pixel-level spacing/typography deltas vs the source are NOTES for the refine pass — record them, do not fail.

steps.name: Theme 4/6 — homepage sections
steps.prompt:
Build the homepage. Using clone-manifest.json's homepage section inventory, compose `home_page/default/index.liquid` from the base theme's canonical section library (heroes, image_text_split, feature_grid, featured_products, testimonial_grid, faq_accordion, cta_banner_v2 …) — call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") for the library list and section rules. Prefer canonical sections; only write a custom section when nothing in the library fits, following the full Section Shell + Container pattern.

Requirements:
- If a homepage section needs a COLLECTION to render (e.g. featured_products' collection picker), create the needed collection(s) NOW via POST /api/company/v1/collections (idempotent: GET first, skip existing; set product membership via PATCH /api/company/v1/products/{id} with {product:{title,collection_ids:[...]}} — the PATCH must include title or it 422s). The later content-import step reconciles the full set; do not wait for it.
- Every source homepage section is represented, in source order, with REAL scraped copy and DAM image URLs from the manifest — no lorem ipsum, no hotlinked source-CDN images.
- Content lives in blocks (richtext for text, canonical image blocks for images); template schema carries sections + order + settings ONLY (never blocks data).
- Tokens, not hex: colors via the background_colors option group, fonts via font_families.
- Audit gate: `python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` on every touched file — fix every violation.
- Verify with screenshot_preview at desktop and mobile; compare against the manifest's source notes and record deviations as refine notes.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: sections used (canonical vs custom), audit result, and the deviation notes list for the refine pass.
acceptance: The homepage renders in the dev preview without server/Liquid errors and contains a section for every entry in the manifest's homepage inventory, in source order (verify against the manifest, not the worker's claim).
Sections use real scraped copy + DAM images — spot-check: no lorem/placeholder text in hero/features, no pointing at the source site's CDN.
`python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` passes on the homepage template and every new/modified section file.
Desktop + mobile screenshots were taken this turn and the page is structurally coherent at both widths (no blank page, no stacked garbage).

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only for a broken/blank homepage, a missing majority of sections, placeholder content standing in for real copy, or unfixed audit violations. Spacing/size/color deltas vs the source are refine-pass NOTES.

steps.name: Theme 5/6 — product & collection templates
steps.prompt:
Build the product and collection surfaces — the catalog was imported BEFORE the theme track, so verify against REAL products. Call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") for template rules (Phase 5) and the canonical PDP/collection section list.

Requirements:
- `product/default/index.liquid`: lead with the canonical product-data section that wires Fluid's product object + add-to-cart (`product_hero` in the current base theme; `main_product` in older scaffolds — use whichever the scaffold ships, NEVER a hand-rolled replacement and never modify `sections/main_product`), then match the SOURCE PDP's section structure from the manifest (benefits, ingredients, how-to-use, reviews, related — whatever the source uses) with canonical product_* sections. This one default template drives every PDP.
- `collection/default/index.liquid` (+ `collection_index` if the source has a collections/shop index) using canonical collection sections. Remember: Liquid's `collections` global has a different shape than the REST API (see the skill's gotchas).
- Verify in the dev preview with REAL data: GET /api/company/v1/products, open at least one real product's PDP route and one collection route, screenshot both. If the run has no products (products out of scope or manual stub), verify the templates render the placeholder/empty state cleanly and note it.
- Audit gate: `python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` on all touched files.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: templates written, which real product/collection routes were verified with screenshots, audit result, refine notes.
acceptance: product/default/index.liquid leads with the scaffold's canonical product-data section (product_hero or main_product — unmodified, not a hand-rolled replacement) and adds source-matching sections after it; collection/default exists and renders.

At least one REAL product PDP and one collection route were loaded in the dev preview this turn without server/Liquid errors, with screenshots (or, when the catalog is legitimately empty for this run scope, the empty state renders cleanly and is noted).
`python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` passes on the touched files.
HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only for erroring PDP/collection routes, a replaced/modified main_product section, or unfixed audit violations. Fidelity gaps vs the source PDP layout are refine-pass NOTES.

steps.name: Theme 6/6 — content pages, full audit & push
steps.prompt:
Finish and ship the theme. Call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") for Phases 5-7.

1. Content page templates: from clone-manifest.json's page manifest (max 4 key static pages — about/faq/contact/policies), build `page/<slug>/index.liquid` templates with the scraped copy + DAM images. (Page RESOURCE records are created later by the content-import step — templates only here.)
2. Full-theme audit: `python3 scripts/theme_audit.py "$THEME_DIR"` across the whole theme — fix EVERY violation; the theme does not ship with violations.
3. Push: `fluid theme push` from the theme dir (honoring `theme_target_resolved` from clone-manifest.json — `existing` pushes to that theme_id). If the CLI push fails, fall back to the resource API per the skill.
4. Verify after push: dev preview still healthy (screenshot_preview), and GET /api/application_themes confirms the landing theme exists; record its id.
5. Aggregate every 'refine note' recorded by theme steps 1-5 plus your own into a single `remaining_for_refine` list.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: theme id, pages/templates shipped, audit summary (0 violations), push result, and the aggregated remaining_for_refine list the refine step will consume.
acceptance: `python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` across the theme exits 0 — zero violations shipped.
The theme was pushed: GET /api/application_themes shows the landing theme and STEP_OUTPUT records its id (verify via the API, not the worker's claim).
The dev preview renders after the push (screenshot this turn) — no server errors introduced by the push.
Key static page TEMPLATES from the manifest exist (up to 4); STEP_OUTPUT carries the aggregated remaining_for_refine list.

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only when the push did not land (no theme id verifiable via the API), audit violations remain, or the preview is broken after push. A shorter-than-hoped page list or a long remaining_for_refine list is fine — the refine pass exists for that.

steps.name: Iterative screenshot-based theme refine
acceptance: Phase A CODE-parity gate ran FIRST and reported CODE_PARITY: pass before any screenshot round: per-template structural comparison vs the source (sections present + ordered), brand tokens (no hardcoded hex/fonts), lint clean (no Liquid errors in the dev server log), and every template route renders. Screenshots are the granular FINAL pass — a run that started pixel-diffing before code parity does not satisfy this step.
The skill ran the source-vs-clone screenshot loop and reported STATUS: pass OR STATUS: cap-reached — either is acceptable; a silent loop is not.
The STEP_OUTPUT names the pages verified this run and, if not passing, lists remaining majors and minors so the launch-readiness review can pick them up.
The theme's dev preview is still healthy — verify with a final screenshot_preview after refinement completes.
HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only when the refine loop never ran, the preview is left broken, or the report is a silent/fabricated pass. cap-reached with an honest majors/minors list is a PASSING outcome.

steps.name: Import every page as a resource (collections, categories, pages, posts, menus)
steps.prompt:
Create EVERY page on the source site as its Fluid RESOURCE — not just products (products are handled by products-import), and not just templates (the theme steps copied the layouts). Two axes must both be satisfied: (1) each page/URL on the source becomes a Fluid resource record, and (2) each page-type template was shipped by the theme track. This step owns axis (1) for non-product content. Follow the `fluid-product-admin-import` skill for the exact payloads.

FIRST: if context flag `import_products` is not true, emit STEP_OUTPUT { skipped: true, reason: 'content out of scope' } and return.

Enumerate the full source site (sitemap.xml + crawl — or reuse the theme track's clone-manifest.json page manifest when present) and, for each URL, create the matching resource — idempotent (GET-before-POST, skip existing, no duplicates):
- **Collections** → POST /api/company/v1/collections (with product membership). Exclude $0 app-helper/internal collections (subscription tiers, ymal/crosssell, test) — see the skill's junk-filter note.
- **Categories** → POST /api/company/v1/categories, ONLY if the source has a curated category taxonomy distinct from collections (else skip, correct-by-design).
- **Static pages** (/pages/*: about, faq, contact, shipping, policies, etc.) → create a page resource for each. Use the pages endpoint per the skill (note: POST /api/company/pages currently works; the /v1/pages variant may 404 pending a fix — do not build a client-side fallback). The theme was already pushed by the theme track — that is why this step depends on it (page creation auto-generates theme templates a later theme push would delete).
- **Blog posts** (/blogs/*/*) → POST /api/posts for each published article (title, body, hero image via DAM, date, slug). If the source blog has 0 published articles, that's correctly 0.
- **Menus / nav** → POST /api/menus to mirror the source header/footer navigation so links resolve.

Space out page-create bursts (WAF throttles them). After creating, RE-COUNT each type via its list endpoint (meta.pagination.total_count) and reconcile against the source. End with STEP_OUTPUT: { collections:{source,created}, categories:{...}, pages:{source,created}, posts:{...}, menus:{...}, skipped_junk:[...], remaining_for_human:[...] }.
acceptance: If import_products was not selected, the step correctly skipped and did no work.

Otherwise: every source collection (minus $0 app/internal junk), every curated category (or justified none), every static /pages/* page, every published blog post, and the site nav/menus were created as Fluid resources — reconciled against the source via each type's list-endpoint total_count (report exact source-vs-created counts per type).
Creates are idempotent (GET-before-POST, no duplicates on re-run); legitimately-empty types (e.g. no blog articles) are justified, not fabricated.
STEP_OUTPUT reports per-type source-vs-created counts and any remaining_for_human items.

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only when a whole resource TYPE that clearly exists on the source was never attempted, duplicates were created, or counts were fabricated. Per-item failures (a page create 403'd by the WAF, one post failed) recorded in remaining_for_human are notes, not failures.

steps.name: Reconcile onboarding info
steps.prompt:
Reconcile the company's server-side onboarding record with what this run actually produced. NOTE: the legacy checklist endpoints (`/api/v1/onboardings`, `check_step`, `complete_step`) are REMOVED from api.fluid.app — they 404. Do NOT chase them. The live surface is:

1. Resolve the active company id (GET /api/me → company.id, or /api/settings/companies).
2. GET /api/companies/{id}/onboarding_info — read what's on file (country_code, countries_info, entity, settlement currency, business fields).
3. Cross-check against the gather-context step's output: for any field the run gathered with HIGH confidence that is empty on the record (e.g. country/entity basics), PATCH /api/companies/{id}/onboarding_info with just that field. Never overwrite non-empty values; never push LOW-confidence data. KYC/payments fields that require human/legal input are ALWAYS deferred, never fabricated.
4. Report: fields already set, fields this step filled, fields deferred to the human with reasons ('requires payments KYC', 'requires legal entity docs', 'human decision').

This step is best-effort reporting — an honest 'endpoint returned <status>, nothing writable' report with the exact request/response is a VALID outcome. End with STEP_OUTPUT: { onboarding_info_read: true|false, fields_set:[...], fields_filled:[...], deferred:[{field,reason}], endpoint_notes:[...] }.
acceptance: The step made a real GET /api/companies/{id}/onboarding_info call this turn (or documented its exact failure status) — the report cites concrete fields from the actual response, and does NOT call the removed /api/v1/onboardings endpoints.
No non-empty server value was overwritten; nothing LOW-confidence or KYC-sensitive was pushed; every deferred field has an explicit reason.
STEP_OUTPUT follows the documented shape with fields_set / fields_filled / deferred.

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only for fabrication (claiming reads/writes the API doesn't show) or destructive overwrites. 'Read-only outcome, everything deferred to the human' is a PASSING outcome when reported honestly.

steps.name: Discover TikTok / UGC content for the DAM
steps.prompt:
FIRST: if context flag `discover_ugc` is not true, emit STEP_OUTPUT { skipped:true, reason:'discover_ugc not selected' } and return. NOTE: this is OTHER PEOPLE's content about the brand (UGC); the brand's OWN channel content is the separate brand-social-import step. Otherwise proceed.

Find user-generated and social content for this company and load it into the Fluid DAM. This step is best-effort — a company with no discoverable social presence is a valid outcome.

1. From the gather-context step's output, pull TikTok / Instagram handles. If none were found there, run one tiktok_search with the company name as a keyword to double-check.
2. If no handles and no keyword hits: emit a short 'no discoverable UGC presence — queries attempted: [...]' report and return. This is acceptance, not failure.
3. Otherwise, for 3-8 promising videos, use the video_ripper tool to download and dam_upload to push into the company's DAM. Tag uploads with the brand name from gather-context.
4. Report every DAM asset URL you created.
acceptance: Either at least one UGC asset was uploaded to the DAM (verifiable via its reported URL), or an explicit finding documents no discoverable social/UGC presence with the queries tried.
No unrelated or off-brand content was uploaded.

steps.name: Import the brand's own YouTube + TikTok content
steps.prompt:
FIRST: if context flag `import_brand_social` is not true, emit STEP_OUTPUT { skipped:true, reason:'import_brand_social not selected' } and return (passes QA as a correct skip). Otherwise follow the `marketing/brand-social-import` skill exactly.

Imports the COMPANY'S OWN social video content — NOT UGC. (1) Resolve the company's official YouTube + TikTok accounts from gather-context social links / the site footer (confirm via tiktok_search user-mode only if unlinked — never import an unconfirmed account); (2) register confirmed handles via PATCH /api/settings/social_media (GET first, don't clobber); (3) enumerate each account's videos (TikTok: tiktok_search mode:user; YouTube: channel uploads RSS); (4) rip each via video_ripper (DAM + Media in one call) tagged `brand-content,<platform>,<brand>` — idempotent, skip already-imported, never abort on one failure. Report accounts registered, videos found/ripped/skipped/failed with DAM URLs.
acceptance: If import_brand_social was not selected, the step correctly skipped (STEP_OUTPUT skipped:true) and did no work.
Otherwise: official accounts were resolved (site links, or search-confirmed — no unconfirmed accounts) and registered via PATCH /api/settings/social_media.

Otherwise: each account's videos were ripped into DAM + Media tagged `brand-content` (never `ugc`), idempotently, per-video failures noted without aborting; or an explicit finding documents no discoverable official social presence.
No UGC / other-people's content was imported by this step (that is ugc-discovery).

steps.name: Verify links resolve to the right resource templates
steps.prompt: Audit EVERY link in the storefront and make each point to a valid, correctly-rendering Fluid resource template — this is the step that catches nav items wired to dead or generic routes. Cover: the header navigation, the footer (support / legal / social / localization), and primary in-page CTAs (hero, category tiles, banners). For each link, resolve the target and confirm it (a) returns HTTP 200 and (b) renders the CORRECT template: collection links -> collection template, category -> category, page -> page, product -> /home/products/<slug>, home -> home. FIX links that point to: a dead or generic route (e.g. a bare `/shop` that 204s instead of `/home/shop`), the wrong template, a Shopify-style URL that doesn't map to Fluid's `/home/...` routes, or a 302/404/406. Navigation menu items MUST map to real resources — e.g. 'By Scent' -> a collections/scent index (`/home/collections`), NOT a generic shop URL; 'Best Sellers' -> `/home/collections/best-sellers`; 'Gifts & Sets' -> `/home/collections/sets`. Prefer binding the nav to a real Fluid navigation menu (link_list) with correct resource URLs so it stays admin-manageable; otherwise correct the hrefs. Point footer info links at the imported pages (`/home/pages/<slug>`). Product-detail pages may 500 platform-side on some stores — that is NOT a link bug: just verify the link SHAPE is the correct `/home/products/<slug>` and do not fail the step on the 500 itself. End with STEP_OUTPUT containing a table: link label -> target URL -> HTTP status -> resolved template.
acceptance: Every header-nav, footer, and primary in-page link resolves to HTTP 200 and the correct resource template (product-detail pages excepted — they may 500 platform-side; those only need the correct `/home/products/<slug>` link shape).
No link points to a dead/generic route (e.g. a bare `/shop`), a Shopify-style URL, or the wrong template type.

Navigation menu items map to real resources (By Scent -> a collections/scent index, Best Sellers -> the best-sellers collection, Gifts & Sets -> the sets collection), ideally via a bound Fluid navigation menu rather than hardcoded hrefs.
STEP_OUTPUT includes the link-audit table (label -> target -> HTTP status -> resolved template).

steps.name: Product price QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — PRICES ONLY. Visit EVERY product's PDP (enumerate via GET /api/company/v1/products) and confirm the displayed RETAIL price and, where a subscription plan exists, the SUBSCRIPTION price render on the page and MATCH the API variant data for the store's default country (variant_countries.price / subscription_price). Flag any PDP where the price is missing, $0, or differs from the API. If the store serves MULTIPLE countries, switch the storefront country (or request with the country's locale) for at least a couple of products and confirm the price + currency update correctly to that country's variant_country pricing. Do NOT check anything else (links, cart, layout are other steps). STEP_OUTPUT: a table of product -> displayed retail / subscription price -> API expected -> match?, plus any mismatches and the country-switch check result.
acceptance: Every PDP shows a non-zero retail price that matches the API variant price for the default country.
Subscription price is shown on products that have a subscription plan, and matches the API.
For multi-country stores, at least one country switch is verified to change the displayed price + currency correctly (or the report states the store is single-country).
STEP_OUTPUT lists every product's price check and names any mismatch.

steps.name: Add to cart QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — ADD TO CART ONLY. Visit EVERY PDP and confirm the add-to-cart button is correctly wired through FairShare: `data-fluid-add-to-cart="<variantId>"` is present and the id is a REAL active variant of that product; on multi-variant products it is VARIANT-AWARE (selecting a scent/size updates the button's variant id + price); `data-fluid-quantity` and `data-fluid-open-cart-after-add` are sane. Confirm the cart drawer/FairShare SDK is present (the `fluid-cdn-script` is injected). Flag any PDP with a missing, hardcoded, placeholder, or stale variant id, or a non-variant-aware selector. Do NOT check prices/links/layout. STEP_OUTPUT: a table of PDP -> data-fluid-add-to-cart value -> real active variant? -> variant-aware?, plus any failures.
acceptance: Every PDP has a data-fluid-add-to-cart bound to a real, active variant id for that product.
Multi-variant products update the add-to-cart variant id (and price) when a variant is selected.
No PDP has a missing, placeholder, or stale variant id.
STEP_OUTPUT lists every PDP's add-to-cart wiring and names any failure.

steps.name: Mobile responsive QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — MOBILE ONLY. Using Playwright at a mobile viewport (390x844, deviceScaleFactor 2), visit one of EACH sitemap route type — home, a collection, a category (if any), a product PDP, a content page, and the cart — and confirm each is ready for mobile traffic: NO horizontal overflow/scroll (document.scrollWidth <= viewport width), the header nav collapses to a working mobile/hamburger menu, tap targets are adequately sized (>=40px), images scale within the viewport, and text is readable (no tiny/overflowing type). Screenshot each route at mobile width. Flag any route with overflow, an overlapping/cut-off section, a broken mobile nav, or unreadable text. Do NOT check prices/cart-wiring/link-targets. STEP_OUTPUT: a table of route -> mobile status -> issues, with screenshot paths.
acceptance: No sampled route has horizontal overflow at 390px width.
The header navigation has a working mobile (hamburger) state.
Primary CTAs/tap targets are adequately sized and images scale within the viewport.
STEP_OUTPUT includes a per-route mobile check with screenshots and any flagged issues.

steps.name: Product active-status QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — PRODUCT STATUS ONLY, and run this BEFORE the price/add-to-cart QA (they depend on it). The Fluid Products API can create products as `status: "draft"` when the create payload omits `status: "active"` — the switch is `PATCH /api/company/v1/products/{id}` with `{product:{status:"active"}}`. A draft product 404s its PDP and is hidden from its membership collections, which silently breaks the storefront and every downstream QA. Enumerate ALL products (GET /api/company/v1/products) and confirm each has `status == "active"` (not draft/scheduled/archived). For any product still draft, PATCH it to active. Then confirm each product's PDP renders 200 and the product appears in at least one collection it belongs to. Do NOT check price/cart/layout (other steps). STEP_OUTPUT: count of products by status, list of any drafts you activated, and PDP + collection-membership render confirmation for a sample.
acceptance: Zero products remain in draft/scheduled — every imported product is status == active.
Every product's PDP renders 200 (not 404 from a draft).
No collection is left with only draft members.
STEP_OUTPUT reports the status counts and any drafts activated.

steps.name: Storefront route health QA (browser-only)
steps.prompt: Focused QA — ROUTE HEALTH, BROWSER-ONLY. Assert the home index AND one of EACH resource type — a collection, a category (if any), a product PDP, a content page, and the cart — returns HTTP 200 with a non-trivial rendered body. CRITICAL METHODOLOGY: use a REAL headless browser (Playwright) for every status check. DO NOT trust curl / HTTP-client status codes: prod Cloud Armor / the WAF returns 500 / 302->404 to non-browser clients EVEN WITH a browser User-Agent, while a real browser gets 200. If a route fails only under curl but renders 200 in Playwright, it is a WAF/bot artifact, NOT a defect — report it as healthy and do not chase it as a platform bug. Only a route that fails IN A REAL BROWSER is a real problem. STEP_OUTPUT: a table of route type -> URL -> Playwright HTTP status -> rendered? , and an explicit note that curl status was disregarded.
acceptance: Every sampled route type (home, collection, category, PDP, content page, cart) renders HTTP 200 with a non-trivial body IN A REAL BROWSER (Playwright).
Any route that fails only under curl but passes in-browser is identified as a WAF/bot artifact, not flagged as a bug.
STEP_OUTPUT reports the per-route-type browser status and states that curl status was disregarded.

steps.name: SEO metadata QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — SEO METADATA ONLY (browser-based). For each route type (home, a collection, a product PDP, a content page), load it in a real browser and assert the <head> + document are SEO-ready: a non-empty, resource-SPECIFIC <title> (NOT empty and NOT a generic storefront default like 'Live Free.'), a meaningful <meta name=description> (not the generic default), a <link rel=canonical>, and exactly ONE <h1> with real resource content. Product and collection pages should also emit the relevant JSON-LD (Product / ItemList / BreadcrumbList). Fix what the THEME controls (title/description/canonical/h1/JSON-LD in the layout + templates, driven by the resource drop — e.g. `{{ page_title }}`, product/collection fields). FLAG what only store-level SEO settings can fix (site-wide default title/description, robots) for the human. STEP_OUTPUT: a per-route-type table -> title / description / canonical / h1 / JSON-LD present? -> pass/flag.
acceptance: Every route type has a non-empty, resource-specific <title> (not a generic default) and a meaningful meta description.
Every route type has a <link rel=canonical> and exactly one <h1> with real content.
Product and collection pages emit the relevant JSON-LD.
Theme-controllable gaps are fixed; store-level SEO-setting gaps are flagged for the human. STEP_OUTPUT lists the per-route SEO check.
Each PDP <title> contains the product name; if Fluid's layout scope makes product unavailable so the title falls to the brand default, flag it for the human rather than leaving it silently generic.

steps.name: Page route content QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — CONTENT PAGE ROUTES ONLY (browser-based). For every content/info page the onboarding authored (About, Contact, Shipping, Privacy, Terms, FAQ, Store locator, etc.), load /home/pages/<slug> in a real browser and assert the AUTHORED BODY renders — not just the nav + footer chrome. A page whose main region is empty means a page RECORD was never created (a template alone does not route content). CREATE the missing record via POST /api/company/pages (note: /api/company/v1/pages and /api/pages both 404 — use /api/company/pages), then re-check; html_code compiles async so re-GET/re-PATCH if the body returns empty, and use a FRESH slug (deleting a page tombstones its slug). Confirm every footer/nav link that points at a /pages/ route lands on a page with real body copy. STEP_OUTPUT: a table of page slug -> record exists? -> body renders? -> linked-from resolves? -> pass/fixed/flag.
acceptance: Every authored content page renders its real body copy in a browser, not just nav + footer.
Missing page records are created via POST /api/company/pages (fresh slug) and re-verified.
Every footer/nav link to a /pages/ route resolves to a page with real content.
STEP_OUTPUT lists per-page record-exists / body-renders / linked-from status.

steps.name: Font substitution QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — FONT LICENSING & SUBSTITUTION ONLY. Determine the source brand's primary display + body typefaces. If a source font is proprietary (not OFL/Google-hosted/freely licensable) and was substituted with a free alternative, assert the substitution is done honestly and completely: (1) the closest free family is used consistently across the theme (no lingering references to the proprietary family name), (2) a license disclaimer naming the original font and the free substitute is embedded in the theme (e.g. a comment in layouts/theme.liquid), and (3) a sane font-stack fallback is present so text never renders in an unstyled default. If the brand's own licensed font files ARE importable (this is their store), import the real @font-face and keep the disclaimer noting the licensing assumption. STEP_OUTPUT: source font(s) -> proprietary? -> substitute used -> disclaimer present? -> fallback present? -> pass/flag.
acceptance: Source typefaces identified; any proprietary font that was substituted is called out.
Substitute family is applied consistently with no leftover proprietary-family references.
A license disclaimer (original + substitute) is embedded in the theme and a fallback stack is present.
STEP_OUTPUT lists per-font substitution + disclaimer + fallback status.

steps.name: Launch-readiness review
steps.prompt:
Produce a live-verified launch-readiness report. This is NOT a summary of what earlier steps said — every claim here must be backed by a check YOU performed this turn.

1. **Storefront live check** — from the gather-context step's context, find the company's public storefront URL (from /api/settings/companies/{id}). crawl(<url>, formats: ['screenshot']) and confirm it returns without error. Attach the screenshot's URL to the report.
2. **Theme sanity** — screenshot_preview once to confirm the theme's dev preview still renders. Read the iterative-theme-refine step's STEP_OUTPUT for any remaining majors/minors and surface them.
3. **Products** — GET /api/company/v1/products and count via meta.pagination.total_count. Spot-check 3 for non-empty title + price + at least one image. Flag any product whose title matches 'Sample Product' — that's the manual stub and it must not ship.
4. **Onboarding info** — GET /api/companies/{id}/onboarding_info (the legacy /api/v1/onboardings endpoints are removed — do not call them) and record what business/country info is on file vs still missing. Compare to what populate-getting-started reported; flag drift.
5. **Brand + business info** — GET /api/settings/brand_guidelines and confirm the brand color tokens from gather-context landed. If a token is still default/empty, flag it.
6. **Degraded steps** — if any earlier step finished in a degraded/needs-review state (its findings appear in your context), fold its unresolved findings into the checklist below with appropriate severity.
7. **Prioritized checklist** — assemble a `Before you launch:` list. Each entry has:
   - severity: `blocker` (unlaunchable), `high` (embarrassing at launch), `medium` (fix week 1), `low` (nice-to-have)
   - what: one line
   - why: which check this turn produced it
   - suggested action

Rank by severity. If there are zero blockers and ≤ 2 highs, say so plainly — the report is not required to invent problems.
acceptance: The report cites live checks performed THIS turn: at least one GET /api/company/v1/products, at least one GET /api/companies/{id}/onboarding_info (never the removed /api/v1/onboardings), and either a crawl-screenshot of the public storefront or an explicit 'storefront URL not yet published' note.
The 'Before you launch' checklist exists and every entry has severity + what + why + suggested action.
Any remaining majors from iterative-theme-refine's STEP_OUTPUT (and any degraded/needs-review step findings present in context) appear in the checklist with severity assigned.
The manual-stub product 'Sample Product' is either flagged as a blocker (Case C ran) or explicitly noted as absent (Case A/B ran).
